title: Registry overview
purpose: Choose the next action available to your Registry account.
steps:
Open Households or Individuals for published records.
Open Registration review to track submissions, or Approvals for assigned review work.
requirements: Counts reflect the selected register and your access.
next_step: A draft, a pending submission and a published master record represent different stages.
source: Registry UI and approval screens · registry-ui-source

title: Registration and field work
purpose: Start a field registration or follow a submission you own.
steps:
Choose the household or individual registration option available to your account.
Use the draft or pending queue to continue an existing submission.
Field staff can use Offline field capture when it is offered.
requirements: Check which register is selected before opening a queue.
next_step: After Level 1 approval, the record leaves the field workspace. A returned record becomes available to correct when assigned back to you.
source: Registry UI and approval screens · registry-ui-source

title: Assigned Registry reviews

Open My registration reviews or My change request reviews.
Check the task type and current review stage before opening the submission.
requirements: Your role and assignment determine which decisions are available.
next_step: Use the earlier decision and history when handling a later review stage.
source: Registry UI and approval screens · registry-ui-source

title: Household registry
purpose: Find published household records and inspect their details.
steps:
Search the household list and open the matching record.
Check the identifier and members before opening a detail or change request.
requirements: Use the published register to look for the current master record.
next_step: Follow unfinished submissions from Registration review.
source: Registry UI and approval screens · registry-ui-source

title: Individual registry
purpose: Find published individual records and inspect their details.
steps:
Search the individual list and open the matching record.
Check the available sections and linked household where shown.
requirements: Use the correct individual identifier to distinguish similar results.
next_step: Open version history when you need to distinguish current and earlier values.
source: Registry UI and approval screens · registry-ui-source

title: Published household details
purpose: Inspect the current household record and its linked information.
steps:
Check the household identifier and open the relevant details section.
Review members and any related change requests before proposing a correction.
requirements: A change request goes through the configured review process.
next_step: Use Approval history for decisions and Record version history for committed changes.
source: Registry UI and approval screens · registry-ui-source

title: Published individual details
purpose: Inspect the current individual record and any linked household information.
steps:
Check the record identifier before reading or proposing an edit.
Choose the relevant detail section or open Record version history to see committed changes.
requirements: Submit an authorised correction through the change request controls shown to your account.
next_step: A pending proposal and the published record can show different values.
source: Registry UI and approval screens · registry-ui-source

title: Record version history
purpose: See the values and changes recorded for a published Registry record.
steps:
Open the relevant version.
Compare it with the current record or another version, where available.
Use change request history to identify how a proposal was reviewed.
requirements: Confirm the record identifier and version before comparing.
next_step: Use the current published value for later operational work.
source: Registry UI and approval screens · registry-ui-source

title: Register a household
purpose: Save a household record and send the completed registration for review.
steps:
Record the respondent’s consent and complete the location and household member sections.
Save each changed section. Use Save Draft to finish later.
Check the whole record, tick the household accuracy confirmation and choose Submit.
requirements: Use the approved collection procedure and confirm the correct register.
next_step: If submission is blocked, resolve the named fields or unsaved sections before submitting.
source: Registry UI and approval screens · registry-ui-source

title: Register an individual
purpose: Capture and submit a registration in the individual register.
steps:
Complete the sections shown for the individual.
Save each changed section and resolve validation messages.
Review the record before choosing Submit. Use Save Draft to continue later.
requirements: Check that you are working in the Individual register.
next_step: Follow the submission in Registration review after it has been sent.
source: Registry UI and approval screens · registry-ui-source

title: Survey consent and enumeration
purpose: Record the response to the consent question for this interview.
steps:
Explain the request using the approved consent wording.
Select the response the person gave. The option No — stop the interview tells you to stop.
requirements: Confirm the applicable consent wording and data collection procedure with the programme owner.
next_step: Use the escalation route approved for refusal or uncertainty.
source: Registry UI and approval screens · registry-ui-source

title: Household location

Confirm the matching State/FCT, LGA and ward and save the section.

next_step: When the device cannot get a fix, retry outdoors or use the available manual entry.

title: Health and vulnerability information

Choose the response that matches the interview and use any follow-up fields shown.

next_step: Escalate uncertain classifications through the programme’s approved procedure.

title: Household income

title: Household assets and crops

title: Start a data import
purpose: Load structured records from an authorised file or configured connection.
steps:
Choose the Data source and expand Expected columns.
For an uploaded file, choose CSV or XLSX and select Validate file. For a configured connection, use Fetch and validate to retrieve its CSV.
Open Reconcile records before requesting approval.
requirements: Files can contain up to 2 MB, 1,000 data rows and 40 columns. XLSX uses the first worksheet. Keep identifiers as text to preserve leading zeros. Extract and verify scanned or PDF data before preparing a structured file.
next_step: If validation lists missing headers, fix the file and start a new import.
source: Live Master Registry Data Imports catalog release and 19 November Data Imports testing guide
issues: For the hosted synthetic pilot, select Synthetic Data Imports test only and use fictional rows with Reference and Test note headers.

title: Fetch and validate a connected CSV
purpose: Retrieve the latest CSV from the selected connection and validate it using the saved source mapping.
steps:
Choose the connected Data source and check Expected columns.
Select Fetch and validate. A new fetch opens a draft with the source and mapping version. After a lost response, use the same Registry login and source from either browser to reopen the saved batch. Both browsers can reopen the same batch if they retry together.
Open Reconcile records. Compare source and mapped values, then save any corrections or exclusions before sending for approval.
requirements: The connection must be configured and active. The CSV can contain up to 2 MB, 1,000 data rows and 40 columns.
next_step: Use the same draft through approval and the Data Bridge transfer. If it is returned, correct that batch and send it for approval again.
issues: For a sandbox test, select Synthetic connected CSV test only. Its headers are Reference and Test note. The fixture includes two versions of the same reference to exercise duplicate validation.
source: Hosted synthetic connected CSV and live Master Registry Data Imports fetch and validation workflow

title: Resolve a connected CSV fetch error
purpose: Recover when the connection is unavailable or Data Imports cannot read the response.
steps:
Note the selected source, error and time. Use the same Registry login and select the same source under New import. Use Fetch and validate to reopen a saved batch whose response was lost. This works from another browser, including when both browsers retry together. If the workspace asks you to choose a match, open Transfers. Select Refresh history and use the batch reference because connected batches can share a filename.
When the batch is reopened, continue from its current status. Use Fetch a new CSV only when you intend to start a separate import from that source. Repeat that action from the same earlier batch to find its separate import. To resume the original, open it by reference in Transfers.
If the fetch never saved a batch, use the same action again once the source is available. Ask the integration administrator to verify the endpoint, credentials and CSV response if the error persists.
requirements: The endpoint requires HTTPS and a CSV response. Integration administrators check any server-side access credential.
next_step: Continue from the existing batch’s current status. Review a draft in Reconcile records. For a batch already sent to the Registry, check or refresh its receipt in Transfers.
source: Live Master Registry Data Imports connector response and error handling

title: Continue with the separate CSV draft
purpose: Identify the separate draft and the earlier batch it belongs to.
steps:
Compare Batch reference if both browsers used Fetch a new CSV from the same earlier batch. Both browsers open the same separate draft. Use one browser to reconcile the rows and Send for approval.
If the browsers started from different originals, each opens its own separate draft even when the source and filename match. Check Previous batch reference before sending either draft for approval.
Open Transfers to find the earlier batch by reference. Choosing Fetch a new CSV from the separate draft starts another import.
next_step: After independent approval, use Transfer to Registry on the selected batch and follow its existing Registry receipt.
source: Hosted concurrent connected CSV fetch verification

title: Choose which connected CSV batch to resume

steps:
Open Transfers and select Refresh history. Use Batch reference to identify the batch you intend to resume. Connected imports can share a source, filename and time.
When different originals have separate drafts, use Previous batch reference to match each draft to its original batch. Open the intended batch and continue from its status. Each batch has its own review, transfer and Registry receipt.
next_step: Continue from the selected batch’s status. Check its rows before approval or refresh its existing receipt if it was sent.

title: Reconcile a saved Registry row with a missing receipt log
purpose: The Registry saved the row and recorded that save in the same transaction. The normal receipt log is still missing for the indicated row.
steps:
Open Reconcile records and check Registry saved, receipt log missing. Use Download audit report and keep the original batch and Registry references.
Field Agent: Report the missing receipt log to the Registry Administrator. Keep the saved row out of follow-up corrections.
First Reviewer: Keep the existing approval and use the original and alternate batch references to follow the reconciliation.
Registry Administrator: Compare the saved-row evidence with the native job and receipt log. If both retries have ended and the log is still missing, keep the failed attempts with the incident evidence. Coordinate with Registry integration support to retry the existing native job once the log error is resolved. Refresh the original receipt to verify the restored log.
requirements: A saved row continues to block alternate transfers for its source key. Native retries reuse the same saved row and share the same receipt, even if they overlap. If another worker is still retrying when a worker fails, keep the alternate blocked and refresh the original receipt when the retry settles.
next_step: Resolve the missing log against the original transfer. After both retries fail, ask Registry integration support to retry that same job once the log error is resolved. Keep the saved row out of alternate batches throughout.
source: Native Registry import save journal and receipt reconciliation

title: Verify a restored Registry receipt log
purpose: The Registry restored the normal receipt log for a previously saved row on the original transfer.
steps:
Check the original Registry reference and confirm Registry logged under Reconcile records. In Activity, look for Registry receipt log restored. Use Download audit report to retain that event.
Field Agent: Keep the restored receipt and leave alternate transfers for the same row on hold.
First Reviewer: Preserve the existing approval and link the restored receipt to the original and alternate batch references.
Registry Administrator: Verify the restored log against the original job and saved-row evidence. If retries overlapped, confirm one receipt-log entry per saved row. If one worker failed after another restored the log, confirm the job stays Processed. If a later retry restored the log after both earlier retries failed, verify Processed and keep the earlier failures with the restored receipt and audit report. If a retry reaches an already Processed job, refresh the original receipt. Confirm the same Registry reference, the existing saved row and receipt log, and a single restoration event. If two retries reach the completed job at the same time, use the same checks and ask Registry integration support to verify both deliveries against the original reference. If one of those retries fails, verify that the original job still shows Processed and the alternate stays blocked. If the first retry fails while the other is still running, refresh the original receipt. Confirm the job is still Processed with one receipt log, then repeat the check after the other retry finishes. Keep the failure details in the integration incident record with the original Registry reference.
requirements: Retries use the original save and job reference. The attempt count can increase while the row and its receipt stay single. If a retry succeeds after an earlier worker failure, the job becomes Processed and clears the earlier job error. Once the job is Processed, any later worker failure stays in worker diagnostics. The logged row continues to block a matching alternate correction.
next_step: Use the original receipt and Registry reference for any follow-up. Where the source creates registrations, follow the relevant registration decisions separately.
source: Registry retry and restored receipt reconciliation

title: Read a Registry receipt when the native job fails
purpose: The Registry logged all included rows before the native job ended with an error.
steps:
Compare the ingested count with the included rows. Under Reconcile records, confirm Registry logged for each affected row. Record the batch reference and native Registry reference with Download audit report.
Field Agent: Keep the receipt and report the job error to the Registry Administrator. Any alternate correction for a logged row stays blocked.
First Reviewer: Keep the existing approval and link its evidence to the received rows.

next_step: Refer the reversal through the authorised reconciliation process. A corrective payment requires an authorised decision. If this is a corrective payment that has also reversed, keep both submitted lists and payment references on the case and escalate before any further payment attempt. After both payments reverse, check the authorised case decision. A further payment goes through a new approval list. Closure records the disposition and ends payment follow-up for the case. If the reversal arrived after case closure, route the new evidence through the authorised reopening process using the same case reference. If a reopened case has a separate payment authorisation, follow it through a new approval list and keep all earlier reversals linked to the case. If a payment authorised after reopening also reverses, retain its report and statement entries with the existing case. Use the authorised process to resolve the new exception. If the CEO closes the reopened case, retain every submitted list and reversal record under the same case reference and follow the recorded closure disposition. If the bank reports the same reversal again, confirm the underlying movement with Finance before changing the case balance or closure status. For an already recorded reversal on a second statement, verify the bank movement and retain both receipt references with the first reversal. If a later statement reports a different reversal amount for the same instruction, use Resolve a reversal amount discrepancy and refer the bank evidence to Finance.

title: Coordinate reversal follow-up
purpose: Connect the reported reversal to the original programme, cycle and approved list.
steps:
Check the programme, cycle and revision against the submitted list and Verification history.
Keep the original approved list and payment reference in the case record.
Give Payment and Finance the list, envelope and batch references through the authorised follow-up process.
requirements: The submitted payment report supports refresh and download. List correction and sponsor bank routing are locked for this submission.
next_step: Coordinate supporting information for the reconciliation owner. Route any proposed corrective action through the authorised process. If this is a corrective payment that has also reversed, link both submitted lists, their revisions and both envelope and batch references in the existing case. Notify Payment and Finance that the case remains open. If the CEO authorises another payment, prepare a separate disbursement list and link it to the decision and both reversals. If the CEO closes the case, archive both submitted lists and their references with the closure record. If a reversal is recorded after case closure, request reopening under the same case reference. Link the newly reversed payment and the closure decision to the existing case. If a new payment is authorised after reopening, prepare a separate list for the authorised amount. Link the reopening, new authorisation and earlier reversal records to that list under the existing case reference. If that newly authorised payment also reverses, keep the reopened case active during review and link the new reversal and bank reason to its approval, envelope and batch. If the CEO closes the reopened case, archive all submitted lists and payment references with the new closure decision and retain the earlier closure and reopening records. If the bank reports a possible duplicate after closure, log the confirmed duplicate under the existing case reference and retain the closure decision. Send unmatched evidence to the reconciliation owner. If the amounts differ, log the amount discrepancy under the existing case reference. Attach both statements and the approved list, envelope and batch references.

If this is a corrective payment that has also reversed, put further payment attempts on hold. Send both payment reports and the case reference to Finance for escalation. If another payment is authorised, submit only the newly approved list after routing and final approval. If the case is closed, stop further payment attempts and retain both reports with the case reference. If a reversal is recorded after case closure, refresh and download the affected envelope report, send it to Finance, and hold further submissions while the case is reviewed. If a new payment is authorised after reopening, submit only the newly approved revision once sponsor bank routing is ready. Track its new envelope and batch in the case. If that newly authorised payment also reverses, hold further payment attempts for the reopened case. Download the latest report and give Finance the new payment references. When the CEO closes the reopened case, end further payment activity for the closed case. Retain the reports under the same case reference. When a possible duplicate arrives, refresh and download the existing envelope report and share both bank notices with Finance. Keep payment activity stopped for the closed case. If a later statement shows a different reversal amount, keep payment activity on hold while Finance verifies the amount. Share both bank statements and the current PBMS report.
source: Installed PBMS payment report controls and submitted-list permissions. Operational follow-up for validation under the agency’s reconciliation procedure.

title: Reconcile the reported reversal
purpose: Determine the financial impact using the reported reversal and the matched statement entry.
steps:
Compare the reconciled and reversed counts with the approved totals.
Match the statement entry to the relevant payment reference and verify the amount and effective date against the bank evidence available to you.
Record the discrepancy and the reconciliation disposition through the authorised process.
requirements: A reconciled count can include a reversed instruction. Check the individual evidence before recording the outcome.
next_step: Share the reconciliation summary with the designated reviewer or decision owner. Preserve the original list, revision and references. If this is a corrective payment that has also reversed, match both payments and both reversals against the bank statement. Confirm the net amount and any unresolved difference, then send the reconciliation summary for an authorised decision. If another payment is authorised, validate the newly authorised amount against the reconciliation and check the new list. If the case is closed, record the final reconciliation outcome and any residual exception in the case. If a reversal is recorded after case closure, match the new bank statement entry, recalculate the case balance across all linked payments and reversals, and submit the updated reconciliation for reopening review. If a new payment is authorised after reopening, verify all linked payments and reversals against the updated case balance and check the new authorised amount. Reconcile the new instruction separately. If that newly authorised payment also reverses, match the new debit and reversal, verify the statement amount, date and reason, and update the reconciliation for the case. For closure after reopening, record the final case balance after matching each payment and reversal, and document any remaining difference and its disposition. For a possible duplicate, compare the bank transaction reference, amount and value date against the reversal already matched to this instruction. Verify the bank movement before recording the original reversal once in the case total. Investigate any difference in the entry or totals. Compare both statement references when a repeat entry arrives on a separately issued statement. For the same movement on a second statement, check that the report still counts the first reversal once and retain both statement references in the case. If the values differ, record the original amount, the later amount and the difference. Verify the movement and effective date with the bank before using either figure to update the case balance.
source: Installed PBMS payment report controls and submitted-list permissions. Operational follow-up for validation under the agency’s reconciliation procedure.

title: Verify reversal evidence
purpose: Review the evidence that links the reversal to the approved revision and original payment.
steps:
Use Refresh report and Download report to capture the current envelope evidence.
Compare the reversal and linked batch references with the approved list, approval history and available statement evidence.
Keep the evidence with the related issue or audit record through the approved process.
requirements: Use the submitted revision to identify what was authorised and what actually occurred.
next_step: Escalate any missing or inconsistent evidence to the designated owner for resolution. If this is a corrective payment that has also reversed, preserve both approval histories and match each envelope, batch and bank statement entry to its submitted list. Escalate gaps in the chronology or evidence. If another payment is authorised, trace the new list to the decision and both prior reversals. If the case is closed, verify the closure evidence and retain both approved revisions with their payment and reversal references. If a reversal is recorded after case closure, preserve the original closure decision and evidence. Verify the late reversal against the affected approval, envelope, batch and bank statement before reviewing the reopening. If a new payment is authorised after reopening, trace the closure, reopening and payment authorisation to the new list. Keep each prior approval and reversal reference available for review. If that newly authorised payment also reverses, retain the new approval and reversal trail alongside the earlier decisions. Verify both the new payment and the reversal evidence. For closure after reopening, verify the full decision history, including the earlier closure, reopening, new authorisation and final closure. Link each submitted revision and reversal to the case. For a possible duplicate after closure, preserve the original closure and retransmission evidence. Check the payment, bank movement and duplicate confirmation against the original reversal. For a confirmed duplicate on a second statement, verify that the first reversal reference is preserved and attach the second receipt to the audit record. For a later statement with a different amount, preserve both statements and the original closure decision. Trace both entries to the submitted instruction and retain the bank confirmation.
source: Installed PBMS payment report controls and submitted-list permissions. Operational follow-up for validation under the agency’s reconciliation procedure.

title: Review the reversal escalation
purpose: Review the reversal with the Finance reconciliation summary and Audit evidence.
steps:
Confirm the affected payment references and the outcome established by Finance.
Review the proposed response through the organisation’s authorised decision or escalation process.
Record the resulting direction in the approved process with the supporting evidence.
requirements: Refresh or download the envelope report when reviewing the escalation. The existing approval history identifies the submitted revision.
next_step: Any corrective payment requires a separate authorised decision and the applicable review process. If this is a corrective payment that has also reversed, review Finance and Audit evidence for both payments and record the escalation decision through the authorised process. The prior approval applies only to the submitted corrective list. To authorise another payment, record the scope and amount of the new authorisation in the authorised case process. To close the case, record the closure decision and reason with the final reconciliation and Audit evidence. Approve and save applies to the current PBMS list revision. If a reversal is recorded after case closure, review the updated Finance and Audit evidence and record the reopening decision, reason and assigned follow-up through the authorised case process. A further payment requires its own authorised decision and approvals. If another payment is warranted after reopening, record a separate payment authorisation with its amount, scope and reason in the authorised case process. The new list then needs its own Finance, Audit and CEO approvals. If that newly authorised payment also reverses, review the new exception under the reopened case and record the next disposition. Any further payment requires its own authorisation and approvals. To close the reopened case, use the updated Finance reconciliation and Audit evidence to record the new closure decision and reason under the same case reference. Include the date and disposition. If the bank reports a possible duplicate after closure, keep the existing closure if Finance confirms the duplicate. Review any new movement or unresolved difference through the authorised case process. If Finance confirms that the later statement shows a different amount, review the unresolved amount before deciding whether to reopen. Record the disposition under the existing case reference.
source: Installed PBMS payment report controls and submitted-list permissions. Operational follow-up for validation under the agency’s reconciliation procedure.

title: Process an authorised corrective payment
purpose: Follow the approved corrective decision while keeping the original reversal and any new PBMS payment traceable.
steps:
Confirm the authorised decision and its case reference, affected instruction and approved amount. Keep the original list revision, envelope, batch and reversal evidence on the case.
If the authorised procedure calls for a PBMS disbursement, Programme Admin prepares a separate list in the authorised programme and cycle. Record the link to the original reversal using the approved case record or available reference fields.
Payment initiates approval of the separate list. Finance checks the amount and reversal evidence, Audit checks the approval trail and references, and CEO records the final list decision under the configured workflow.
Once the separate list is Fully verified and routing is configured, Payment reviews its beneficiary count, total and revision in the confirmation and submits it through the normal payment action.
Finance and Audit compare the new envelope and batch with the corrective approval and reconcile the new instruction separately. Keep both sets of references. Escalate a further reversal through the authorised process.
requirements: An authorised corrective decision and its supporting evidence are required. PBMS keeps the original submitted list available for review and uses its regular approval flow for the separate list.
next_step: Record the new dispatch and reconciliation outcome in the corrective case while retaining the original reversal evidence. If the corrective payment is reversed, follow the escalation guidance for a reversed corrective payment and hold further payment attempts pending an authorised decision.
source: Installed PBMS list approval, payment and reporting controls. The corrective decision and record-keeping steps are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Escalate a reversed corrective payment
purpose: Use the existing case reference when a separately approved corrective payment also has a recorded reversal. In the envelope report, an instruction can count as both reconciled and reversed.
steps:
Programme Admin links both submitted lists, their revisions, envelope and batch references, and payment and reversal references to the existing case.
Payment refreshes and downloads both envelope reports, gives Finance the case reference and supporting reports, and holds further payment attempts pending an authorised decision.
Finance matches each payment and reversal to its bank statement entry, verifies the amounts, dates and reasons, and records the net amount and any unresolved difference.
Audit checks both approval histories and the links between each approved revision, instruction and reversal. Preserve the evidence for both payments in the case.
CEO reviews the Finance reconciliation and Audit evidence and records the decision through the authorised escalation process. Any further disbursement needs a separate authorised decision and the applicable approvals.
requirements: Both submitted lists and approval histories, both envelope and batch references, the relevant bank statement entries, and the existing case reference. Use Refresh report or Download report to collect evidence from PBMS.
next_step: Keep the case open pending the authorised decision. If another payment is authorised, follow Process a further payment after two reversals. If the decision is to close, follow Close a case after payment reversals. Record the decision under the authorised case process. If a reversal arrives after closure, use Reopen a closed case after a late reversal and keep the original closure decision.
source: Installed PBMS report controls and Bridge reconciliation of a synthetic reversal on a separately approved corrective list. Role handoffs are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Process a further payment after two reversals
purpose: Use this route when the authorised case decision permits a further disbursement after the original and corrective payments both reversed.
steps:
CEO records the decision, reason, scope and amount under the authorised case process. Keep the decision reference with the case reference, Finance reconciliation and Audit evidence.
Programme Admin prepares a separate disbursement list for the authorised programme and cycle. Link its revision to the decision and both reversed payment records. Use the approved sponsor bank route.
Payment uses Initiate approval and includes the escalation decision reference. Finance validates the authorised amount and both reversals. Audit checks the links and prior approval history. CEO records final list approval in PBMS.
Once this separate list shows Fully verified and routing is ready, Payment uses Proceed to payments and checks the count, amount and revision before choosing Confirm and proceed.
Finance and Audit track the new envelope and batch independently. Record their references and final reconciliation in the existing case alongside both reversed payments.
requirements: Use the authorised case reference, CEO decision reference, both earlier lists and bank reconciliation evidence. Preserve both submitted lists under their existing payment references.
next_step: Follow the new payment to reconciliation and update the case with its outcome. Route a further exception through the authorised case process. If the new payment reverses after case closure, follow Reopen a closed case after a late reversal and hold any further submissions pending an authorised decision.
source: Installed PBMS list approval, submission and reporting controls. Case authorisation and role handoffs are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Close a case after payment reversals
purpose: Use this workflow when the authorised decision closes a case after payment reversals, including a case that was reopened and had a further payment reverse.
steps:
Finance matches each payment and reversal to its bank statement entry, verifies the amounts, dates and reasons, and records the final case balance. Record the approved disposition for any remaining difference.
Audit verifies all submitted revisions, approval histories, envelope and batch references, and the bank statement evidence. For a reopened case, verify the earlier closure, reopening and any subsequent payment authorisation as part of the same decision history.
CEO records the closure reason, date and disposition in the authorised case process. For a reopened case, add a dated closure decision under the existing case reference and retain the prior decisions.
Programme Admin archives the closure with all submitted lists and payment references. Payment ends further payment activity for the closed case and retains the reports.
requirements: Use the existing case reference, final Finance reconciliation, Audit evidence and the recorded CEO closure decision. Close report in PBMS dismisses the report window. Record case closure through the authorised case process.
next_step: Keep all submitted lists and payment reports available for audit with their original approval and reversal records. If a later statement records a new reversal, follow Reopen a closed case after a late reversal under the same case reference. For a retransmitted reversal, follow Handle a duplicate payment reversal. Keep the existing closure when Finance confirms the same bank movement. Use the reopening process for a genuinely new reversal or another exception that requires a case decision. If a later statement gives a different amount for an existing reversal, follow Resolve a reversal amount discrepancy before making a new case decision.
source: Installed PBMS reversal reporting and submitted-list controls. Case closure and role handoffs are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Reopen a closed case after a late reversal
purpose: Use this workflow when a bank statement records a reversal against a payment after the case was closed. The PBMS envelope report can show the instruction as both reconciled and reversed.
steps:
Payment refreshes and downloads the affected envelope report, records the list, revision, envelope and batch references, and gives the evidence to Finance. Hold further payment submissions.
Finance matches the late statement entry to the affected instruction. Check the amount, effective date and reason, then recalculate the net balance across all linked payments and reversals. Record any unresolved difference.
Programme Admin requests reopening under the existing case reference. Attach the late reversal evidence, the updated Finance reconciliation and the original closure decision.
Audit verifies the chronology from approval through dispatch, reconciliation, closure and late reversal. Keep the original closure evidence and trace each payment to its own submitted revision, envelope, batch and bank statement entry.
CEO reviews the Finance and Audit evidence and records the reopening decision, reason, date and follow-up owner in the authorised case process. Keep any later payment decision separate from reopening.
requirements: Use the same case reference and retain the closure decision, all linked approval histories, payment and reversal references, and the new bank statement evidence. PBMS reports provide Refresh report and Download report. Record reopening through the authorised case process.
next_step: Update the reopened case with the reconciliation outcome and assigned follow-up. A further disbursement requires separate authorisation and the applicable list approvals. When a separate payment authorisation is recorded, follow Process an authorised payment after case reopening.
source: Installed PBMS payment report controls and Bridge reconciliation of a synthetic statement reversal after test case closure. Case reopening and role handoffs are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Process an authorised payment after case reopening
purpose: Use this workflow when the CEO records a separate payment authorisation after a reversal case is reopened. Keep the reopening and payment decisions under the existing case reference.
steps:
CEO records the new payment decision, scope, amount and reason through the authorised case process. Reopening restores case follow-up. A separate authorisation is required for a new payment.
Programme Admin prepares a separate disbursement list in the authorised programme and cycle. Link the new list to the case reference, reopening decision, new authorisation and each earlier payment and reversal. Configure the approved sponsor bank route.
Payment initiates approval of the new list with the case and decision references. Finance verifies the net balance and authorised amount. Audit traces the decisions and earlier payment records. CEO records final approval of the new list revision.
After the new list shows Fully verified and routing is ready, Payment compares the beneficiary count, amount and revision with the authorisation. Use Proceed to payments and Confirm and proceed for that approved list.
Finance matches the new instruction to its bank statement entry. Audit preserves the new envelope, batch and reconciliation outcome alongside the earlier payment records and the closure, reopening and authorisation decisions.
requirements: Use a reopened case reference, a dated reopening decision, a separate payment authorisation, the updated reconciliation, and the prior approval and reversal evidence.
next_step: Record the new reconciliation outcome in the existing case. Use the authorised case process for any subsequent exception or closure decision. If the statement records another reversal while the case is reopened, keep the case active during review. Payment holds further attempts. Finance matches the debit and reversal, verifies the amount and reason, and updates the case balance. Audit retains the new approval and reversal trail. CEO reviews the new exception and records the disposition through the authorised case process. If the CEO decides to close the reopened case, follow Close a case after payment reversals and retain the earlier closure, reopening and payment authorisation.
source: Installed PBMS list approval, submission and reporting controls. Reopened case decisions and role handoffs are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Handle a duplicate payment reversal
purpose: Review a bank reversal that may already be recorded on the same PBMS instruction, including after case closure.
steps:
Payment refreshes and downloads the existing envelope report. Share the original and latest bank notices with Finance, along with the approved list, revision, envelope and batch references. Keep payment activity stopped for the closed case.
Finance matches the payment instruction and bank transaction reference, amount and value date to the reversal already reconciled. Check the original and latest statement reference. An exact resend can reuse the original receipt. When Bridge accepts a second statement for an instruction with a recorded reversal, it keeps the first reversal and its count. Compare the bank entries to confirm that the second receipt refers to the same movement. Compare both statement references even when the PBMS totals appear consistent. If reversals exceed reconciled instructions, log a report discrepancy and verify the case balance from the matched bank evidence.
If the same movement is confirmed, use the original reversal once in the case total. Audit retains the original closure, bank evidence and duplicate confirmation. Programme Admin logs the repeat receipt against the existing case reference.
If evidence indicates a new movement or an unresolved difference, document the discrepancy and route it through the authorised case process. CEO reviews the Finance and Audit evidence and records any required decision on reopening.
requirements: Use the existing case reference, the original payment and reversal evidence, and the latest bank evidence. The PBMS envelope totals can support the review. Confirm duplication from the bank entries.
next_step: Keep the existing closure once the duplicate is confirmed. Follow the authorised reconciliation process for an unresolved difference or a separate reversal. When the amounts differ, use Resolve a reversal amount discrepancy and record the disagreement while Finance verifies the bank movement. Bridge records a reversal amount exception when the amounts differ or the original amount cannot be verified.
source: Installed Bridge statement processing and PBMS reporting verified with an exact resend and a separate statement from the local Example Bank. Case decisions and role handoffs are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Investigate a reversal count discrepancy
purpose: The envelope shows more reversals than reconciled instructions. Compare the report with the matched bank evidence before using the totals.
steps:
Refresh and download the envelope report. Record the approved list, revision, envelope and batch references.
Ask Finance to compare the original and latest statement entries and confirm whether they describe the same bank movement.
requirements: Use both statements when a repeat appears on a separately issued statement. The count discrepancy is a signal for review.
next_step: If the case is already closed, hold payment activity while the discrepancy is reviewed through the authorised process.
source: Installed Bridge reversal processing and PBMS reports. Count discrepancies verified in synthetic browser responses. Case decisions and role handoffs are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Log the reversal discrepancy
purpose: Keep the reported discrepancy and the closure history traceable to the same case.
steps: Attach the latest PBMS envelope report and both statement references to the existing case reference. Record the referral to Finance and Audit.
requirements: Keep the previous closure decision and the submitted list references with the new evidence.
next_step: Use the Finance and Audit findings to update the authorised case record. Route any reopening decision through the authorised process.
source: Installed Bridge reversal processing and PBMS reports. Count discrepancies verified in synthetic browser responses. Case decisions and role handoffs are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Hold payments while Finance checks the reversal totals
purpose: The reversal count exceeds the reconciled count. Confirm the statement evidence before any further payment activity.
steps: Refresh and download the report for the same envelope. Share it with Finance along with both bank statement references, the approved list and the batch.
requirements: Keep the current payment, list and envelope references with the referral.
next_step: Hold further payment activity while Finance confirms the bank movement and resolves or escalates the discrepancy.
source: Installed Bridge reversal processing and PBMS reports. Count discrepancies verified in synthetic browser responses. Case decisions and role handoffs are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Investigate the reversal count discrepancy
purpose: The report totals need verification against the bank entries before they are used in the case balance.
steps:
Match the original and latest statement entries to the same instruction. Compare the bank transaction reference, amount and value date and verify whether a new bank movement occurred.
Record a confirmed duplicate once in the case balance. Log any remaining difference between the report count and the bank evidence.
requirements: Use the original reversal, latest statement and downloaded envelope report for the comparison.
next_step: Share the reconciliation and any unresolved discrepancy with Audit and the authorised decision owner.
source: Installed Bridge reversal processing and PBMS reports. Count discrepancies verified in synthetic browser responses. Case decisions and role handoffs are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Preserve evidence of the reversal count discrepancy
purpose: Preserve the original reversal evidence and the later report with the discrepancy.
steps: Keep both statement references, the original closure and the latest report. Trace each entry to the instruction, approved revision, envelope and batch. Review the Finance conclusion and document the evidence for any unresolved difference.
requirements: Keep the original approval and closure history with the evidence for the late statement.
next_step: Refer an unresolved difference to the authorised decision owner for a documented disposition.
source: Installed Bridge reversal processing and PBMS reports. Count discrepancies verified in synthetic browser responses. Case decisions and role handoffs are provisional for agency procedure validation.

title: Review the reversal discrepancy before deciding on reopening
purpose: Use the Finance and Audit findings to determine the disposition for an already closed case.
steps: Review whether the statements show the same bank movement and whether the discrepancy has been resolved. Keep the closure when the duplicate is confirmed and the discrepancy is resolved or handled under the authorised process.
requirements: Refer a confirmed new bank movement or an unresolved exception through the authorised case process. The report count alone calls for reconciliation review.
next_step: Record any required case decision and the reason under the existing case reference. Further payment requires separate authorisation and the applicable approvals.

title: Resolve a reversal amount discrepancy
purpose: Use this when Bridge flags a later reversal with a different amount or cannot verify the first amount. Number Of Reversal Amount Exceptions can increase while the reconciliation and reversal counts stay the same.
steps:
Payment keeps further activity on hold for the closed case. Refresh and download the report and give Finance the two bank statements, the existing case reference and the approved list, envelope and batch references.
Finance matches the instruction, currency, value date and bank transaction references. Record the original reversal amount, the later reversal amount and the difference. Confirm with the bank whether the later entry is a correction, a separate movement or a reporting error.
Programme Admin logs the amount discrepancy under the existing case reference. Audit preserves both statements, the original matched reversal, the approval history and the closure decision. Keep the bank confirmation with the case.
CEO reviews the confirmed bank evidence and any unresolved difference through the authorised case process. Record any decision to reopen under the same case reference. Further payment requires separate authorisation.
requirements: Use both statement references and the first matched reversal. Bridge keeps the first reversal while recording the exception. Compare the bank entries and verify any missing original amount with Finance.
next_step: Keep the original reconciliation as evidence and hold payment activity while the discrepancy is reviewed. Record the verified amount and the case disposition through the authorised process.

title: Review a reversal amount exception

requirements: The Number Of Reversal Amount Exceptions field counts recorded exceptions for this envelope. Use both bank statements to verify the amount and disposition.

title: Reconcile the flagged reversal amount

title: Trace the reversal amount exception

requirements: The Number Of Reversal Amount Exceptions field counts recorded exceptions for this envelope. Use both bank statements to verify the amount and disposition.

steps: Review the unresolved amount before deciding whether to reopen. Record the decision, reason and owner under the existing case reference through the authorised process.
requirements: The Number Of Reversal Amount Exceptions field counts recorded exceptions for this envelope. Use both bank statements to verify the amount and disposition.

title: Prepare an import for approval
purpose: Complete the validation and reconciliation checks on a draft.
steps:
Read the four counters and checked mapping version.
Expand rows with issues. Correct a source value or exclude a row, then Save row and verify the mapped result.
Use Send for approval once there are included rows and their validation checks pass.
requirements: Missing headers require a corrected file and a new import. The operator works on their own batch.
issues: If a connected fetch retry reopened this draft, continue here. Use Fetch a new CSV only to start a separate import from that source.
next_step: Track Awaiting approval or any return in Transfers.
source: Live Master Registry Data Imports catalog release and 19 November Data Imports testing guide

title: Track an import awaiting approval
purpose: The submitted batch is with the assigned first reviewer.

title: Track a queued Registry import
purpose: The native Registry accepted the batch into its import queue.
steps:

requirements: Queue acceptance confirms delivery to the queue. Row ingestion completes separately.
next_step: Continue on the same batch once the native receipt updates.

title: Reconcile a partially ingested import
purpose: The Registry logged only part of the transferred batch.
steps:
Use Refresh Registry receipt on the original batch. Compare the ingested and found counts. Under Reconcile records, select Issues and exclusions only to find included rows marked No Registry row receipt. Clear the filter to see rows marked Registry logged. Excluded rows were outside the transfer.
Field Agent: send the batch reference, Registry reference and affected row numbers to the Registry Administrator.
First Reviewer: compare the outstanding rows with the approved batch and share any discrepancies.
Registry Administrator: reconcile the receipt against the native job and row logs, and coordinate any correction with the integration owner.
requirements: Keep the original receipt and audit report. The Registry worker owns ingestion retries after queue acceptance. Keep the original transfer intact to avoid duplicating rows that were already logged.
next_step: After the integration owner confirms the outstanding rows, use New import for a separate correction file containing only those rows. Keep their existing source keys, link the original batch reference in the evidence, and send the correction through independent approval before transferring it.
source: Live Master Registry Data Imports catalog release and 19 November Data Imports testing guide

title: Report a partial Registry receipt
purpose: Identify which included rows still lack a Registry receipt and report them to the Registry Administrator.
steps:
Select Refresh Registry receipt on the existing batch and compare the ingested and found counts.
Under Reconcile records, select Issues and exclusions only. Note the included rows marked No Registry row receipt. Clear the filter to compare rows marked Registry logged. Excluded rows were outside the transfer.
Use Download audit report to save the evidence alongside the batch and Registry references.
requirements: Keep the original batch and receipt. A partial receipt needs native reconciliation before any further transfer.
next_step: Send the batch reference, Registry reference and outstanding row numbers to the Registry Administrator. After confirmation, use New import with the approved source mapping and a separate file containing only the confirmed outstanding rows. Correct their values, keep their existing source keys, and record the original batch reference in the correction evidence. Send the correction for approval and transfer that batch after approval.
source: Data Imports partial receipt and Field Agent transfer controls

title: Review a partial Registry receipt
purpose: Check whether the Registry receipt accounts for the rows you approved.
steps:
Open the original batch in Transfers and select Refresh Registry receipt. Compare the included rows, the ingested count and the row evidence against the approved batch.
Use Issues and exclusions only to find included rows marked No Registry row receipt. Clear the filter to confirm which rows were logged. Check Activity for the original approval and transfer.
requirements: The original approval remains in the audit trail. The partially ingested batch has no new approval or return action.
next_step: Share any discrepancies with the Registry Administrator. When a separate correction appears under Awaiting approval, compare it with the original receipt and the confirmed outstanding rows. Approve it if it contains only those rows with the expected keys, or return the correction with a reason.
source: Data Imports partial receipt and First Reviewer approval controls

title: Reconcile a partial Registry receipt
purpose: Reconcile the original transfer with the native Registry job and identify any rows that still need action.
steps:
Select Refresh Registry receipt on the original batch. Capture the batch reference, Registry reference, attempts and row counts with Download audit report.
Use Reconcile records to distinguish rows marked Registry logged, No Registry row receipt and Excluded. Compare included row numbers with the native import job and its row logs through the authorised integration owner.
requirements: Preserve the original batch and audit evidence. The native Registry worker owns ingestion retries after queue acceptance.
next_step: Ask the integration owner to confirm the native outcome for each outstanding row. Coordinate a separate correction for confirmed outstanding rows only. Compare the correction receipt against the original receipt and the source keys, then retain both batch and Registry references with the audit reports.
source: Data Imports partial receipt, native row logs and Registry Administrator monitoring controls

title: Resolve a row already in the Registry import pipeline
purpose: An included row has the same source key as a received or in-progress row in another batch using the same source and destination mapping.
steps:
If the warning offers Reload batch, use it to refresh the affected rows. Under Reconcile records, open the row and use Open existing batch when available. Ask the Registry Administrator if your account cannot see that batch.
When two approved corrections try to send the same row, the first transfer reserves it. For Registry transfer in progress, refresh the earlier receipt and wait for its outcome. A received row stays outside any correction file.
requirements: Keep the original source key and evidence. Submission, approval and transfer are blocked while an included row conflicts with an earlier transfer.
next_step: Continue only with rows confirmed outstanding. Check the earlier job for saved-row evidence and receipt logs before reopening an approved correction. Registry receipt needs reconciliation means an earlier result remains uncertain. Keep the hold and ask the Registry Administrator to check it.
source: Data Imports source-key guard and Registry receipt reconciliation

title: Follow a correction blocked by an earlier Registry transfer
purpose: Check the earlier receipt before you continue with the affected batch.
steps:
If the warning offers Reload batch, use it to update the affected rows. Open the affected row in Reconcile records and select Open existing batch when the button is available. Ask the Registry Administrator to verify the receipt if it belongs to another account.
If the status is Registry transfer in progress, select Refresh Registry receipt on the earlier batch and wait for the earlier receipt to settle. Reopen the blocked batch to see the updated row status. If it is Already received by Registry, keep the existing source key and exclude the row from an editable batch.
requirements: An approved batch with a conflict stays blocked from transfer. Ask the Registry Administrator to reconcile the approved batch before taking further action.
next_step: If the earlier correction failed, ask the Registry Administrator to confirm that the native job has ended and check whether the Registry logged the row or recorded its save. A saved row keeps the alternate blocked even if that native job failed. For a confirmed outstanding row, refresh the earlier receipt, then reopen the already-approved correction. If Transfer to Registry is available, transfer that batch and check its receipt. If all rows were already received, leave the repeat batch unsubmitted. Keep the existing receipt.
source: Data Imports Field Agent duplicate receipt controls

title: Check a correction against the existing Registry receipt
purpose: Compare the conflicting row against the earlier receipt before deciding on the correction.
steps: Open the affected row and its existing batch. Compare the source key and receipt. If the earlier transfer is still in progress, wait for its receipt or ask the Registry Administrator to reconcile it.
requirements: Approval is blocked while the correction includes a conflicting row.
next_step: If the correction is Awaiting approval, use Return for correction and give the earlier batch reference and affected row number. If the batch was already approved, send the evidence to the Registry Administrator. If a failed job saved the row, keep the alternate correction blocked and retain the approval evidence. When the earlier transfer fails and the row is confirmed outstanding, check the existing approval and retain both batch references. Review a revised correction only for confirmed outstanding rows.
source: Data Imports First Reviewer duplicate receipt controls

title: Reconcile a blocked repeat Registry row
purpose: Confirm whether the affected source key already has a receipt or is still in a native Registry job.
steps: Open the affected row and the existing batch. Compare the mapped source key, both batch references, the native Registry reference and the row receipt. If two approved corrections competed to send the row, check Activity to confirm which batch entered the Registry queue. Refresh that receipt and coordinate any uncertain outcome with the integration owner.
requirements: A duplicate correction stays blocked from transfer after approval. Preserve the earlier receipt and both audit trails.
next_step: Confirm which rows were already received and share the evidence with the Field Agent and First Reviewer. For failed jobs, check the saved rows and receipt logs. If the job saved the row, keep the alternate row blocked and investigate the existing job. For a confirmed outstanding row, refresh the earlier receipt, then reopen the already-approved correction and check whether the hold cleared. Older jobs without saved-row tracking need native reconciliation before resubmission.
source: Data Imports Registry Administrator duplicate receipt controls

title: Investigate Registry ingestion that needs attention
purpose: The native ingestion job reported a problem after transfer.
steps:
Refresh the receipt and check status, counts, attempts and Registry reference.
Check row evidence and Activity. Refer the batch and queue references to authorised Registry support.
requirements: Confirm the native job is terminal and compare saved-row evidence and receipt logs. A zero count with complete saved-row tracking confirms there are outstanding rows. While the outcome is uncertain, keep any competing transfer on hold.
next_step: If a separate approved correction was blocked and the Registry Administrator confirms the row is still outstanding, refresh this receipt, then reopen the already-approved correction. The authorised Field Agent can transfer it when the action becomes available. Keep both Registry references and audit reports.
source: Live Master Registry Data Imports catalog release and 19 November Data Imports testing guide

title: Check expected import columns

title: Issues and exclusions only

title: Set mapping transforms and required values

title: Field for duplicate checks

title: Correct a source value

requirements: Use the verified source information. If a row should stay out of the transfer, use Exclude this row from the transfer.
source: Live Master Registry Data Imports catalog release and 19 November Data Imports testing guide
